_what_this_is: The screens, section by section, as the owner approved them. This file is the CONTRACT and
the pages are the implementation — not the other way round.
Why it exists (DECISIONS §46). On 17 Sep the dossier was rebuilt from the 16 September artifact
and shipped with 12 of its 25 sections. The test written alongside it pinned those 12 and
passed, because the test was derived FROM THE PAGE I HAD BUILT rather than from the layout the
owner ruled. A check written after the fact can only ever confirm what you already did. That is
how thirteen sections went missing with a green build, and it is the mechanism behind the
owner's complaint that the screens keep changing and degrading.
So the direction is reversed. This file is written from the artifact. scripts/contract_test.ts
reads it and fails when a page is missing a section, renders them out of order, or carries a
section this file does not name. Adding to a screen means adding it HERE first; removing
anything means the owner changing this file. No session can quietly drop a section again,
because the build goes red the moment one disappears.
`required` true means the section must always be in the page's source. Sections that render
only when their data exists are still required HERE: the page must contain the code and the
heading, even if a given account has nothing to put in it.
source_of_truth: The 16 September 2026 artifact, ruled the layout to maintain — DECISIONS §37, §43, §46.

screens.title: The front dashboard
screens.purpose: Every high-level number about the book on one screen, and nothing about one agency. Answers: how big is the book, how well do we know it, what is waiting on a person, and is the machinery actually running.

sections.name: The book right now
sections.shows: companies, records, how many ranked, how many unclassified

sections.name: By anticipated tier
sections.shows: the distribution bar and counts, Platinum through Ungraded

sections.name: Three axes that never touch
sections.shows: tier sets the rank; confidence and engagement are columns — with live counts on each

sections.name: How well we know them
sections.shows: confidence spread and the qualification-facts histogram (0..4 of Dimension A)

sections.name: Never contacted
sections.shows: Gold-or-better with no contact on record — the most actionable number in the book

sections.name: Waiting on a person
sections.shows: fact candidates by why they are queued, and how many can be confirmed together

sections.name: Is the machinery running
sections.shows: last scoring run, last note sweep, the active rubric and its fingerprint, and what moved on the last run

sections.name: What changed on the last run
sections.shows: tier moves, promotions, demotions, newly ranked — the answer to 'did this change under me'

sections.name: What this page is not
sections.shows: no composite score, no forecast; every tier word anticipated and UNVALIDATED

screens.title: The board
screens.purpose: Every prospect ranked by potential. Tier sets the order; whether anyone has called them is a column, never a position.

sections.name: Masthead
sections.shows: count, the lede, and the source line: rubric version, order, row count, live read

sections.name: By anticipated tier
sections.shows: distribution bar and legend with counts

sections.name: Three axes that never touch
sections.shows: tier / confidence / engagement, and that only the first sets the rank

sections.name: The ranked list
sections.shows: grouped headers Potential | Contact; columns rank, company, tier, cell, year one, facts, engagement, they replied

sections.name: Filters
sections.shows: per-tier toggles, never-contacted only, researched only, flagged only, name filter, live count

screens.title: One prospect

sections.name: What we could actually deliver

screens.title: How the grading works

sections.name: What this book decides

sections.name: Signals and how they decay

sections.name: The flags
sections.shows: every flag the engine can raise and what raises it — a flag is a reason to check, never a reason the engine lowered a tier

sections.name: Overrides
sections.shows: the owner lane, the one-tier cap, the reason codes, the expiry, and that a blank expiry still lapses

sections.name: What is still unruled
sections.shows: every open ruling carried as a toggle, with the default it is sitting on today

sections.name: The rules the code keeps
sections.shows: unknown is never evidence; evidence outranks recency and a person outranks a machine; the engine is pure; the rubric is data
